gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a front-plus-rear camera with a 4K Sony STARVIS 2 IMX678 on both channels (Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K) lists at $239.99 on vantrue.com today, $170 under VIOFO's own dual-4K A229 Ultra 2CH ($409.99 on viofo.com) and $20 over the 4K+2K A229 Pro 2CH on Amazon ($219.99); nor that VIOFO's three headline picks cost $70 to $130 more on viofo.com, the prices ChatGPT quoted, than on VIOFO's Amazon listings the same day.
standout_why: Compared against productbible.com (best front-and-rear, VIOFO models compared), thecargearguide.com (A229 Plus vs Pro vs A329S, best front-and-rear) and pacificpartsdept.com (10 cameras compared). Productbible and Pacific Parts already carry the Amazon prices for the A229 Plus, A229 Pro, A329S and A229 Ultra ($159.99 / $219.99 / $373.99 / $299.99), and productbible's VIOFO page already adds hardwire kit totals, so the Amazon side is not new. None of the five pages names the Vantrue S1 Pro Max, DDPAI, Botslab or 70mai with a price, and none sets the viofo.com price beside the Amazon price. thecargearguide gives no dollar prices at all. Car and Driver and Vortex Radar, both cited by ChatGPT, could not be opened (blocked / HTTP 403), so I could not check them.
decides: It confirms the VIOFO A329S 2CH as the top-end pick but changes the middle of the ranking. ChatGPT's 'best balance' A229 Pro 2CH is $349.99 only on viofo.com; on Amazon it is $219.99, and with the HK4 kit $237.98. At that level the Vantrue S1 Pro Max 4K+4K ($239.99, sale price against a $399.99 list) is the honest pick for rear-camera detail: Vantrue's listing names IMX678 sensors front and rear, against a 2K rear on the A229 Pro. ChatGPT gave that slot to the A229 Ultra 2CH at $299.99 (Best Buy), which is $409.99 on viofo.com today. So a Dealectric-linked product places on the question's own terms (4K rear segment), while the A229 Pro on Amazon stays the value pick for a 4K front with a 2K rear.
